messages:
lee: Heads-up: ran the 2k-concurrency replay on staging for release-7. The p99 tail jumped from ~210ms -> 620ms when load hit ~1.8k concurrent requests. Noticed this correlates with a spike in KV cache evictions.
anita: ugh. did the agent pick the fallback kernel or change microbatching?
lee: Microbatch config was the usual: microbatch_size=4, max_batch_delay_ms=6. Kernel selection logs show a few fallbacks to the generic matmul path around the same time.
jon: Can you paste the profiler counters? I want to see KV hit/miss and microbatching stats.
lee: Sure — pasted a short extract from the runtime profiler (truncated):
```
[profiler] concurrency=1800
KVCache: lookups=1,234,512 evictions=12,450 miss_rate=0.241 avg_kv_lookup_ms=0.82
Batching: microbatch_attempts=379k microbatches_formed=94k avg_microbatch_size=4.02
KernelSel: fast_gemm=71% fallback_generic=29% kernel_switch_latency_ms_p95=1.9
serving_latencies_ms: p50=45 p95=180 p99=620
```
maria: miss_rate 24% is big for KV cache. Eviction rate also high. That explains extra reads into the model weight cache and extra KV fetch latency.
anita: Why did fast_gemm drop to 71%? If kernel choices oscillate under varying sequence lengths, we pay the kernel switch cost, which inflates tail.
jon: Two hypotheses:
1) Microbatch_size=4 produces more microbatches -> more scheduling overhead and more concurrent KV slots -> cache pressure.
2) Hot shard imbalances cause localized eviction storms when many requests touch same prefixes.
lee: I instrumented per-shard stats: top-3 shards took 38% of lookups and had 3x higher eviction churn.
maria: Proposed quick mitigations:
- increase microbatch_size to 8 or 12 to reduce scheduling overhead and increase amortization of kernel costs
- increase per-shard KV capacity (or use sampled LFU) for hot keys
- sticky routing for top prefixes
anita: Tradeoffs: increasing microbatch_size reduces CPU/GPU kernel switch overhead and may lower p99 under high QPS, but it can increase p50 for single low-latency requests and increase saturation if bursty.
jon: We tried a quick A/B on a small fleet: microbatch=10, per-shard-kv-cap +20%.
```
A/B summary:
- concurrency: 1800
- microbatch=4 baseline p99=620ms, p95=180ms
- microbatch=10 test p99=320ms, p95=210ms
- KV miss_rate -> 0.12, evictions -55%
```
lee: So p99 improved a lot, p95 slightly worse (from 180 -> 210). Throughput was basically unchanged but fewer kernel fallbacks (fast_gemm=88%).
maria: That aligns: bigger microbatches reduce kernel switching and improve batch efficiency, which short-circuits the eviction cascade because fewer concurrent partial KV windows.
anita: But we can't just bump microbatch globally. Need adaptive microbatching based on inflight and per-route SLOs. Suggest: if route.slo_target_ms < 100 then use microbatch<=2; else if concurrency>1000 then scale microbatch up to 12 with cap.
jon: Also recommend improving KV eviction policy: sampled-LFU + bump capacity for top N shards and add a small soft-reserve for prefix-heavy workloads.
lee: Action items:
- (jon) run a full 24h replay with adaptive microbatching heuristic to see p95/p99 tradeoff across diurnal load — start tonight
- (maria) prototype sampled-LFU eviction for top-shard protection, perf overhead <2% target
- (anita) add telemetry: kernel_switch events correlated with per-request tail flag, and expose per-route microbatch histogram in console
- (dev-bot) create ticket and schedule canary
dev-bot: created ENGRT-5123 — "Adaptive microbatching + KV hot-shard protection to reduce p99 under high concurrency" assigned to jon, maria, anita. ETA next week. :white_check_mark:
maria: One more note — we should also evaluate kernel selection hysteresis (avoid flipping kernels for small sequence-length jitter). Add a 50ms sticky window for kernel decisions.
lee: Good call. If hysteresis reduces kernel_switch frequency we probably get a double win for tail.
anita: I'll draft a config RFC with the heuristic thresholds and A/B plan.
jon: I'll kick off the replay and upload the full profiler dump to the ticket. If anyone wants the quick script to reproduce the heatmap, ping me.
lee: Thanks all — let's iterate. :thumbsup:
